title: Swap Adjacent in LR String
statement:
The strings `start` and `result` have the same length and use only the characters `'L'`, `'R'` and `'X'`. In one move you may pick two neighbouring characters of the current string and either turn `"XL"` into `"LX"` or turn `"RX"` into `"XR"`; no other change is allowed.

Return `true` if some sequence of zero or more moves turns `start` into `result`, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: start and result contain only 'L', 'R' and 'X'
notes:
## Intuition

Read `'X'` as an empty square and each letter as a piece. A move slides an `L` one square left into a gap, or an `R` one square right into a gap. Pieces never jump over each other, so the letters keep their order; an `L` can only end up at or left of where it began, and an `R` at or right. These three facts are also enough: if they hold, the pieces can be slid into place one by one. Searching all reachable strings would work for tiny inputs but explodes quickly.

## Approach

1. Walk `i` over `start` and `j` over `result`, both moving forward.
2. Skip the `'X'`s in each string, so `i` and `j` point at the next piece of each.
3. If either string has no piece left, the answer depends on the other also having none (`i === j` means both reached `n`).
4. The paired pieces must be the same letter.
5. An `L` must not have moved right (`i < j` fails) and an `R` must not have moved left (`i > j` fails).
6. Step past both pieces and continue; return `true` if every pair passes.

## Example 1, step by step

`start = "RXXLRXRXL"`, `result = "XRLXXRRLX"`. The pieces pair up as `R`: 0 to 1, `L`: 3 to 2, `R`: 4 to 5, `R`: 6 to 6 and `L`: 8 to 7. Every `R` stays or moves right and every `L` stays or moves left. After the last pair both pointers skip to `n = 9` together, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each pointer moves forward through its string once.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Comparing only the counts of `L`s and `R`s is not enough; their order matters (`"RL"` cannot become `"LR"`).
- The moves are one-way: `"XL"` to `"LX"` is allowed but not the reverse, so the direction checks are essential.
- When one string runs out of pieces, the other must run out too; trailing pieces mean different letters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of both strings |
| `i` | position of the current piece in `start` |
| `j` | position of the matching piece in `result` |

narration.7: Skip empty squares in start so i lands on the next L or R.
